title: Sound: How We Hear
summary: Vibrations, waves, pitch and loudness, and why there is no sound in space.

steps.title: Sound is a vibration
sentences: Every sound starts with something vibrating, which means moving back and forth very fast.
A drum skin, a guitar string and your own throat all vibrate when they make sound.
Touch your throat while humming and you can feel it.

steps.title: Sound waves
sentences: The vibrating object pushes the air around it, and the push travels as a wave.
Sound needs something to travel through, such as air, water or a solid.
In empty space there is nothing to carry it, so space is silent.

steps.title: Pitch and loudness
sentences: Pitch is how high or low a sound is, and it depends on how fast the vibration is.
A small bell vibrates fast and sounds high, while a large drum vibrates slowly and sounds low.
Loudness depends on the size of the vibration and is measured in decibels.

steps.title: How your ear works
sentences: Sound waves enter your ear and make your eardrum vibrate.
Three tiny bones pass the vibration on to the inner ear.
There the vibrations are changed into signals that your brain understands as sound.
points: The brain makes sense of it

facts: Sound moves about 340 metres per second in air, and much faster in water and steel.
An echo is a sound that bounces back from a hard surface.
Very loud sounds over a long time can damage hearing.

quiz.q: Why is there no sound in space?
options: There is no air to carry the waves
quiz.why: Sound needs a medium to travel through.

quiz.q: A small fast vibration gives a...
quiz.why: Faster vibrations give a higher pitch.
